summary:
**Earth Trends — Tracking Earth's Changes Through Radar Intelligence**

Earth Trends is an interactive Earth-observation platform developed by **APEX LEGENDS** for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. Our project addresses the challenge of understanding environmental changes through NASA-ISRO NISAR satellite radar data and related Earth-observation resources.

We developed a working research demonstration that brings satellite dataset exploration, radar data processing, and scientific visualization into one accessible interface. The platform supports three major research applications: **ground deformation monitoring, flood and surface-water change detection, and vegetation disturbance analysis**.

Earth Trends integrates NASA ASF dataset discovery, SAR processing workflows, interactive geographic maps, and an analysis dashboard to help users explore complex radar information and interpret potential changes on Earth's surface.

Our current demonstration uses synthetic and local test datasets, with clear data-source labeling. Processing and scientific validation using genuine NISAR satellite observations remain part of our ongoing research.

Our goal is to make satellite-based Earth monitoring more understandable, accessible, and useful for researchers, environmental planners, and communities. We are continuously improving the platform's scientific accuracy, reliability, and real-world capabilities.
details:
Earth Trends — Project Details

Developed by APEX LEGENDS | NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026

Earth Trends is an interactive Earth-observation and scientific analysis platform designed to make satellite radar data easier to explore, process, and understand. Developed by APEX LEGENDS for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, our project focuses on the challenge of tracking changes on Earth's surface using data and resources associated with the NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar (NISAR) mission.

What Does Our Project Do?

Earth Trends brings three major Earth-monitoring applications into a unified research platform:

  1. Ground Deformation Monitoring: Uses interferometric radar phase information to estimate line-of-sight ground displacement indicators, helping investigate potential surface movement.
  2. Flood and Surface-Water Monitoring: Analyzes radar backscatter patterns and changes to identify potential surface-water areas and flooding indicators.
  3. Vegetation Disturbance Analysis: Uses radar backscatter and polarization-related indicators to investigate possible vegetation changes and environmental disturbances.

These capabilities are presented through interactive maps, scientific visualizations, and analysis results that help users interpret complex satellite information.

How Does It Work?

Our application follows a modular scientific workflow:

Satellite Dataset Discovery → Data Validation → SAR Processing → Earth Change Analysis → Interactive Visualization

The platform integrates NASA ASF dataset discovery and supports metadata exploration associated with ISRO Bhoonidhi. Compatible locally staged HDF5 products can be passed through processing workflows based on NISAR GUNW interferometric and GCOV backscatter product structures.

Users can explore geographic regions, examine dataset information, configure analysis parameters, execute processing workflows, monitor job status, and inspect results through interactive maps and dashboards.

The application clearly distinguishes synthetic demonstrations, local test fixtures, catalog metadata, and satellite data whose provenance requires verification.

Technologies and Tools Used

We developed Earth Trends using:

  • Python: Scientific computing, backend logic, and satellite data processing.
  • FastAPI: Backend services, data access, analysis execution, and REST APIs.
  • NumPy and h5py: Numerical operations and HDF5 scientific data handling.
  • HTML, CSS, and JavaScript: Interactive web application development.
  • Leaflet.js: Geographic maps and spatial visualization.
  • Chart.js: Scientific graphs and analytical dashboards.
  • GeoJSON: Geographic data representation and export.
  • NASA ASF DAAC and ISRO Bhoonidhi: Satellite data discovery and related resources.
  • Git and GitHub: Version control and collaborative software development.

The application is designed to run on conventional computing hardware, without requiring specialized satellite-reception equipment.

What Makes Our Project Creative?

Our innovation is not the invention of a new radar sensor or satellite algorithm. It is the integration of several complex Earth-observation workflows into an accessible, transparent, and interactive research environment.

Instead of treating satellite data as isolated technical files, Earth Trends connects dataset exploration, scientific processing, geographic analysis, and understandable results within one application.

The platform also emphasizes scientific transparency by distinguishing simulated observations from real satellite products, explaining uncertainty, and avoiding unsupported conclusions.

Benefits and Intended Impact

Earth Trends aims to make Earth-observation technologies more accessible to students, researchers, environmental organizations, and decision-makers.

Its potential applications include understanding ground movement, exploring flood-related changes, and identifying vegetation disturbance indicators.

By simplifying the exploration and interpretation of radar observations, we hope to support environmental awareness, scientific education, and future research into disaster monitoring and sustainable resource management.

Challenges, Considerations, and Future Development

During development, our team considered scientific accuracy, data quality, geospatial alignment, user accessibility, processing efficiency, software reliability, and responsible interpretation of satellite measurements.

We also recognized that radar signals are affected by observation geometry, surface conditions, noise, and other environmental factors. Consequently, our results must be interpreted within documented scientific limitations.

Earth Trends is currently a working research demonstration, with synthetic and local test-data workflows. Independent end-to-end scientific validation using genuine NISAR satellite observations remains an important next step.

Our team is actively improving the platform through further testing, scientific research, interface refinement, and more robust data-processing methods. Future work will focus on real-satellite validation, improved calibration, broader geographic analysis, and increasingly reliable Earth-change interpretation.

Our long-term vision is to develop Earth Trends into a useful scientific tool that helps transform complex satellite radar information into accessible knowledge about our changing planet.

APEX LEGENDS — Think Big. Learn Deep. Build Real.
